strings.name: Bill Clinton
strings.summary: Clinton moved from Arkansas law and governorship into the presidency, serving from 1993 to 2001. His administration advanced North American trade, welfare reform and Balkan diplomacy; economic expansion and budget changes accompanied policy disputes. The Lewinsky affair led to House impeachment in 1998 and Senate acquittal in 1999. He later pursued foundation and global-health work, and in 2026 answered congressional questions about Epstein while denying knowledge of his crimes.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; reviewed on 15 November. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Served two terms as US president, participated in North American trade and Balkan diplomacy, and his administration’s economic and social policies had lasting influence.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Georgetown undergraduate degree (1968); attended Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar without completing a degree there; Yale law degree (1973).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Two presidential terms
strings.highlights.h1.text: Participated in North American trade and Balkan diplomacy and pursued economic and social policies, leaving contested welfare and criminal-justice legacies.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Public affairs after office
strings.highlights.h2.text: Worked on health, development and disaster-relief partnerships through his foundation and Clinton Global Initiative.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Testified to Congress on Epstein ties
strings.timeline.t1.text: Answered questions about his Epstein relationship, denying knowledge of crimes and personal wrongdoing.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Founded Clinton Global Initiative
strings.timeline.t2.text: Established a platform for cross-sector commitments to development cooperation.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Completed presidency
strings.timeline.t3.text: Finished two terms and pursued foundation work.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Acquitted in Senate impeachment trial
strings.timeline.t4.text: The House passed perjury and obstruction articles in 1998; neither obtained the Senate votes needed for conviction.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Welfare reform and reelection
strings.timeline.t5.text: Signed legislation restructuring federal welfare and won reelection; the reform’s effects remain debated.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Advanced Bosnia peace process
strings.timeline.t6.text: His administration helped broker the Dayton agreement and pursued Balkan diplomacy.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Signed NAFTA implementation law
strings.timeline.t7.text: Signed implementing legislation for NAFTA, effective in 1994.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Became US president
strings.timeline.t8.text: Took office as the 42 nd president.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Became Arkansas governor
strings.timeline.t9.text: Previously attorney general; served as governor in 1979–1981 and 1983–1992.
strings.timeline.t10.title: Earned Yale law degree
strings.timeline.t10.text: Returned to Arkansas to teach law before entering electoral politics.
